uses.label: Armenian Catholic Church: patriarchal (Cilician) books
uses.finding: The Vienna 1879 Խորհրդատետր սրբոյ Պատարագին carries a declaration signed by Anton Petros IX (Hassun), Patriarch of Cilicia, dated 6 January 1879, which ties the book to the 1847 Constantinople national assembly held with Holy See permission and to a later decision of the patriarchate's bishops on one uniform Mass book. The title page, declaration and the 388-page lection part were inspected in the acquired scan. A 1904 Vienna second printing in two forms (plenary with lections, and ordinary only) is reported by the Mekhitarist journal Handēs Amsōreay and by the Enciclopedia Cattolica (1951). A revised order effective at Pentecost 1994 is reported by an official retrospective.
uses.limit: The 174-page ordinary section of the 1879 book is not in the delivered scan; the 1904 forms, the 1932 cantor's book and the 1994 book and decree were not seen. No textual delta between 1677, 1879 and 1994 has been collated.
next_sources: A complete copy of Vienna 1879 including its 174-page ordinary (Mekhitarist library, Vienna; NLA Yerevan)
Google Books jJIwAQAAMAAJ (Vienna 1904 plenary) and Handēs Amsōreay 1904 no. 12, bibliography entries 118-119
Աւետիք 1994, p. 365 (patriarchal decree) and the 1994 revised book
uses.review_remaining_gap: The 174-page part of 1879, the 1904 forms, the 1932 cantor's book, the 1994 decree (Աւետիք 1994, p. 365) and book, and any post-1994 book remain unseen; no 1677/1879/1994 collation.

uses.label: Roman (Propaganda Fide) editions for Armenians, 1642-1777
uses.finding: Besides the existing 1642 and 1677 rows, the national bibliography (1512-1800) records a Rome 1777 Khorhrdatetr of the priest's daily prayers, printed 'by command of the superiors', issued together with a 738-page Rome 1777 lectionary (Ճաշոց) into which the Khorhrdatetr is inserted. The bibliography's Rome 1670 entry reproduces the 1642 title and derives its date from Ghazikian citing Brightman, so it is not independent evidence of a 1670 edition.
uses.limit: The 1777 books were known here only through the bibliography and an NLA catalogue search snippet; no page images were seen. Brightman's 'Rome 1686' Uniat edition was not confirmed by any repertory searched.
next_sources: NLA Yerevan and San Lazzaro copies of the Rome 1777 Khorhrdatetr and Ճաշոց
Propaganda Fide printing records for 1686 (Brightman's Rome 1686)
uses.review_remaining_gap: Rome 1777 books unseen; Brightman's Rome 1686 unresolved; Brightman p. xcviii also lists a Latin 'Ordo divinae missae Armenorum Romae 1632' among translations, not accounted for in the packet.

uses.label: Mekhitarist books of Venice (San Lazzaro) and Trieste
uses.finding: The national bibliographies record Venice and Trieste Mekhitarist printings whose titles state that they follow the Rome exemplar (Venice 1741, printed by Bortoli; Trieste 1803; Venice 1809; Venice 1823 in three issues; Venice 1874; Venice 1883 small format), and complementary ministrant books: Սպասաւորութիւն սրբոյ պատարագի (Trieste 1783, 1785, 1803; Venice 1785), low-Mass server books (Trieste 1786; Vienna 1854; Venice 1875, 1889), and the clerks' book Կարգ դպրութեան (Venice 1834, 1857, 1863, 1889), plus combined celebrant-and-clerks books (Venice 1826; third printing 1854).
uses.limit: Bibliographic evidence only, except for the already registered 1823 80-page witness. Several entries are marked by the compilers as not seen. Reprints are not counted as revisions; no collation was performed.
next_sources: San Lazzaro library holdings of the Trieste 1803 and Venice 1809 books
Complete Mekhitarist catalogue of Venice publications (1934, 1960)
uses.review_remaining_gap: All books except arm-1823 unseen; Trieste 1808 (entry 115, unseen, citing Zarbhanalian p. 281 and Ghazikian) and Venice 1808 remain leads; Venice 1895 lead; Mekhitarist Venice catalogues 1934 and 1960 unexamined.

uses.label: Vienna Mekhitarist books (before and after the 1879 patriarchal book)
uses.finding: The Vienna 1858 Khorhrdatetr, printed 'according to the exemplar printed in Rome', was acquired whole (84 images: 64 pages of the Mass order plus a separately paginated 15-page table of Mass lessons and Gospels). The bibliography 1851-1900 also records Vienna books for the low-Mass server (1854), an annual order for deacons and clerks (1877, 456 pages) and a Mass book for deacons and clerks (first printing 1879).
uses.limit: Only the 1858 book was seen. The Vienna 1879 deacons' book is known from a Mekhitarist catalogue cited by the bibliography (entry marked not seen); a publisher price list reports a date of 1880 for what may be the same book.
next_sources: Vienna Mekhitarist library copies of the 1877 and 1879/1880 deacons' and clerks' books
uses.review_remaining_gap: 1877 and 1879/1880 deacons' books unseen; Vienna 1880 ordinary and Vienna 1884 leads unresolved.

Dashian's 1895 catalogue of the Vienna Mekhitarist manuscripts, MS 18

uses.label: Pre-union and shared Armenian manuscript and commentary ancestry
uses.finding: Brightman (1896, pp. xcvi-xcix) lists the Lyon Or. 15 (1314), Munich arm. 6 (1427) and San Lazzaro arm. 1411 manuscripts and ten liturgies or anaphoras no longer in use. Macler (1908) catalogues Paris supplément arménien 50 as an 1858 copy of the 1314 Lyon manuscript with the liturgies of Athanasius, Gregory the Illuminator, Basil, Gregory the Theologian, John Chrysostom and Sahak. The 1897 Vienna edition by Gatrčean and Tašean (Սրբազան Պատարագամատոյցք Հայոց), the Xosrov commentary (Venice 1869) and the Nersēs Lambronac‘i commentary (Venice 1847) were acquired whole.
uses.limit: No manuscript was inspected. The 1897 edition's apparatus and the commentaries' embedded liturgy texts were identified from their title pages but not collated. Winkler's and Feulner's critical editions were not acquired.
next_sources: Feulner 2001 (Athanasius anaphora critical edition)
Winkler 2005, 2011, 2013 (Basil, Sahak, James editions)
Lyon, Bibliothèque municipale Or. 15 images
uses.review_remaining_gap: No manuscript inspected; Feulner and Winkler editions not acquired; 1177 Lambronac'i date and Step'anos text unexamined.

uses.label: Latin-rite books in Armenian (Dominican, Franciscan, Fratres Unitores)
uses.finding: Macler (1908) catalogues two fourteenth-century Roman missals translated into Armenian: supplément arménien 71, translated in 1337 for the Dominicans of the province of Armenia, and ancien fonds arménien 22, translated by the Franciscan Boniface (completed at Avignon in 1344; copied at Bologna in 1381). USUARIUM records a printed Armenian Dominican missal of 1728. Bodleian MS Marshall Or. 106 (c. 1675) is a separate case: an Armenian-rite low-Mass extract for a Roman-Armenian priest.
uses.limit: These Latin-rite books are translations of Western uses; their histories are deferred and they are not counted as Armenian-rite versions. Paris supplément arménien 3 (ff. 109 onward) was not checked.
next_sources: USUARIUM 8323 record and the Greenstone (Fundamental Scientific Library) copy of the 1728 Dominican missal
uses.review_remaining_gap: Paris suppl. arm. 3 unlocated; 1728 Dominican missal unopened; Brightman's modern translations (French Venice 1851, English Venice 1872, Italian Venice 1873, German Tübingen 1845, Latin Rome 1632) are not labelled as deferred witnesses.

uses.label: Armenian Apostolic altar-book sequence (comparison only)
uses.finding: The national bibliographies list Apostolic Khorhrdatetr printings from New Julfa 1641 and Venice 1686 through Constantinople, Smyrna, New Nakhichevan, Echmiadzin/Vagharshapat, Shushi, Tiflis and Jerusalem, up to 1894. Brightman uses Smyrna 1761 and Jerusalem 1873 as base texts.
uses.limit: Catholic reception of these books is not asserted. They are labelled here so that they are not mistaken for Catholic witnesses.
next_sources: Collation of Venice 1686 against Rome 1677 (the 1686 images are now acquired)
uses.review_remaining_gap: Venice 1686 not collated with Rome 1677; Echmiadzin 1873 unresolved; Catholic reception of Apostolic books not asserted.

limits: No research.json existed; everything here was rebuilt from retained files and re-checked. Bibliography entries are bibliographic evidence; only the 1858, 1879 and 1686 books and the four historical editions were opened.

Reprints, issues and complementary books (celebrant, deacons and clerks, low-Mass servers, lectionaries) are kept distinct and grouped into reprint families; none is counted as a revision without collation.

Armenian Catholic and Armenian Apostolic books are separated: Venice 1686, New Julfa 1641 and the 1706-1894 Apostolic printings are comparison witnesses only; the Venice 1686 lectionary's Catholic use rests only on the 1951 encyclopedia.

The arar.sci.am viewer labels the 1858 and 1879 editions 'Secured publication' although their PDFs downloaded without credentials from the page's own citation link. No credentials or circumvention were used, but the root should review whether these bytes may be retained at all; they are proposed restricted.
Vienna 1879 delivered scan lacks the 174-page ordinary; any claim about the 1879 ordinary text rests on the retrospective, not on this scan.
